value: Marshall Elliott married Miss Cornelia Bryant.
unit: Born into a family of staunch politicians, Marshall Elliott vowed during a bitter general election fifteen years prior that he would not cut his hair or shave until his political party, the Grits, came to power. He faithfully kept his vow for fifteen years despite remaining a bachelor and looking peculiar to strangers. During this time, he spent leisure hours with local friends, such as going cod-fishing with Captain Jim and watching the old year out at the lighthouse, where he sang ballads and danced with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won power, he immediately visited the barber before sunrise to be shaved and get his hair cut. Shortly afterward, he married Miss Cornelia Bryant and lived with her for over thirteen years. He also went over-harbour to investigate the mistreatment of the child Mary Vance by Mrs. Wiley, expressing great fury over her abuse.

unit: Matthew lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla, keeping mostly to himself and avoiding public life. In early June, he dressed up and went to Carmody to fetch Anne Shirley, whom he brought home to Green Gables despite his usual fear of strangers. He quickly grew fond of Anne, enjoying her chatter, taking her side during disagreements, and offering her quiet support. He lived a quiet life tilling the fields and tending the homestead until his sudden death caused by the shock of reading about the failure of the Abbey Bank. He passed away instantaneously with a peaceful expression and was buried in Avonlea, where Anne maintained a weekly pilgrimage to his grave long after his passing.

unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea prior to her birth. Later in life, after her daughter Elizabeth married and moved to India as a foreign missionary, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. She agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housekeeper at Patty's Place for Anne, Priscilla, Phil, and Stella, quickly winning their deep affection. While managing Patty's Place, she kept house alongside three cats, including her bed-companion the Sarah-cat, whose purring comforted her worries about snakes in India. After the college girls completed their studies, she eventually traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field despite her dread of snakes.

unit: Philippa Gordon met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant at Redmond College and quickly became close chums with them. Coming from a rich, exclusive Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, her beauty and popularity opened doors for her friends across Redmond's social life. She struggled to choose between her suitors Alec and Alonzo until spending time at Prospect Point, where she fell in love with a minister named Jonas. She moved into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Stella, and Aunt Jamesina, learning household tasks while excelling in her studies. Despite initial resistance from her mother, she stood firm and married Jonas in June after graduating, eventually having children. Later, she advised Gilbert Blythe by letter that Anne was not engaged to Roy Gardner, encouraging him to try again.

label: History
value: The conclusion of her rule at Avonlea school occurred at the end of June.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher in Avonlea school. She introduced innovations to the school curriculum such as alternate Friday afternoon recitations, field days in the woods to study nature, and morning and evening physical culture exercises. After catching Anne Shirley reading a novel tucked inside her Canadian history desk during school hours, Miss Stacy held her back at recess to gently correct her for wasting time and deceiving her teacher, before freely forgiving her. At the end of her first year, despite rumors that she would take a job offer in her home district's grade school, she returned to Avonlea for another term to prepare her older students for the Entrance examinations. During her tenure, she advised ambitious pupils such as Anne and Gilbert Blythe on taking up Second Year work at Queen's Academy. Her rule at Avonlea school concluded at the end of June following her second year of teaching.
